117: > \(c\) Logical access controls, including role-based access control (RBAC) with least-privilege principles, multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all administrative and privileged access, and segregation of duties for critical Processing activities;
118: >
119: > \(d\) Annual penetration testing conducted by an independent third-party information security firm, with findings reported to the Processor\'s Chief Information Security Officer and remediation tracked to completion;
120: >
121: > \(e\) Intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDS/IPS) deployed across all network segments and monitored on a continuous 24/7 basis by the Processor\'s security operations center;
122: >
123: > \(f\) Regular vulnerability scanning conducted on a monthly basis, with critical and high-severity vulnerabilities remediated within timeframes established by the Processor\'s vulnerability management policy, and a formalized patch management program.
124: 
125: **5.3** The Processor shall regularly test, assess, and evaluate the effectiveness of its technical and organizational measures for ensuring the security of Processing, in accordance with Article 32(1)(d) of the GDPR. Such testing and evaluation shall be conducted at least annually and shall include, at a minimum, the penetration testing and vulnerability scanning described in Section 5.2(d) and (f) above.
126: 
127: **5.4** The Processor holds ISO 27001:2022 certification, Certificate Number ISO-27001-SC-2024-0891, issued by TÜV Rheinland AG on June 15, 2024, valid through June 14, 2027. The Processor shall maintain ISO 27001 certification (or an equivalent internationally recognized information security management system certification) throughout the term of this DPA. The Processor shall promptly notify the Controller if its ISO 27001 certification is suspended, withdrawn, or not renewed, and shall provide the Controller with a remediation plan within thirty (30) calendar days of any such event.
128: 
129: **5.5** The Processor shall not materially diminish the overall level of security provided by its technical and organizational measures during the term of this DPA. The Processor may update or modify its technical and organizational measures from time to time, provided that any such update or modification does not result in a material reduction in the level of security afforded to the Controller\'s Personal Data. The Processor shall update Annex B to reflect any material changes to its technical and organizational measures and shall provide the updated Annex B to the Controller within thirty (30) calendar days of such changes.
130: 
131: **[SECTION 6 --- SUBPROCESSING]{.underline}**
132: 
133: **6.1** The Controller hereby provides general written authorization to the Processor to engage Subprocessors for the performance of specific Processing activities on behalf of the Controller in connection with the Services provided under the Agreement, subject to the conditions and requirements set forth in this Section 6. The Processor shall ensure that it engages Subprocessors only to the extent necessary for the provision of the Services and that each Subprocessor is capable of providing sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organizational measures in accordance with the requirements of the GDPR.
134: 
135: **6.2** As of the date of this DPA, the Controller authorizes the engagement of the following Subprocessors, which the Controller acknowledges have been disclosed and are approved:
136: 
137:   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
138:   **Subprocessor**              **Registered Address**                                                **Location of Processing**   **Services Provided**
139:   ----------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------- ---------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------
140:   Larkfield Data Systems, LLC   7600 Prosperity Avenue, Fairfax, VA 22031, United States of America   Northern Virginia, USA       Database management and disaster recovery services
141: 
142:   Orionis Analytics Ltd.        14 Fitzwilliam Square East, Dublin 2, D02 W526, Ireland               Dublin, Ireland              Anonymization and analytics services
143:   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
144: 
145: **6.3** The Processor shall inform the Controller of any intended changes concerning the addition or replacement of Subprocessors, thereby giving the Controller the opportunity to object to such changes in accordance with this Section 6. The Processor shall provide written notice to the Controller at least fifteen (15) calendar days prior to the engagement of any new Subprocessor or the replacement of an existing Subprocessor. Such notice shall identify the proposed Subprocessor, its location, the Processing activities to be performed, and the measures taken to ensure compliance with Applicable Data Protection Law.
146: 
147: **6.4** If the Controller raises a reasonable objection to a proposed new or replacement Subprocessor within the fifteen (15) calendar day notice period set forth in Section 6.3, the Parties shall discuss the Controller\'s concerns in good faith with a view to reaching a mutually acceptable resolution. If the Parties are unable to resolve the Controller\'s objection within thirty (30) calendar days following the Controller\'s written objection, the Controller may terminate the affected Services (i.e., those Services that would require the use of the objected-to Subprocessor) without penalty upon sixty (60) days\' written notice to the Processor. The Processor shall not engage the objected-to Subprocessor for the affected Services during any ongoing objection or termination period.
148: 
149: **6.5** The Processor shall impose on each Subprocessor, by way of a written contract, data protection obligations that are equivalent to those set out in this DPA, in particular providing sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organizational measures in such a manner that the Processing carried out by the Subprocessor will meet the requirements of the GDPR. The Processor shall ensure that each subprocessing agreement includes, at a minimum, the obligations set forth in Article 28(3) of the GDPR, including the obligation to Process Personal Data only on documented instructions, to ensure the confidentiality of personnel, to implement appropriate security measures, and to assist the Controller with data subject requests and breach notifications.
150: 
151: **6.6** The Processor shall remain fully liable to the Controller for the performance of each Subprocessor\'s obligations under this DPA and the applicable subprocessing agreement. Where a Subprocessor fails to fulfil its data protection obligations, the Processor shall remain fully liable to the Controller for the Subprocessor\'s failure as if the Processor itself had performed the relevant Processing activities.
152: 
153: **[SECTION 7 --- INTERNATIONAL DATA TRANSFERS]{.underline}**
154: 
155: **7.1** The Processor shall not transfer Personal Data to any country or territory outside the European Economic Area (\"EEA\") or to any international organization, and shall not permit any Subprocessor to make any such transfer, unless one of the following conditions is satisfied:
156: 
157: > \(a\) The European Commission has issued an adequacy decision for the recipient country, territory, or international organization, or a specified sector within such country, pursuant to Article 45 of the GDPR, and such adequacy decision remains in force and has not been invalidated by the Court of Justice of the European Union or otherwise;
158: >
159: > \(b\) Appropriate safeguards have been provided in accordance with Article 46 of the GDPR, including but not limited to the execution of Standard Contractual Clauses approved by the European Commission, the adoption of binding corporate rules approved by a competent Supervisory Authority, or the use of an approved certification mechanism together with binding and enforceable commitments of the data importer; or
160: >
161: > \(c\) A derogation for specific situations under Article 49 of the GDPR applies, provided that such derogation is interpreted restrictively in accordance with the guidance of the European Data Protection Board.
162: 
163: **7.2** To the extent that the Processing involves transfers of Personal Data from the EEA to the United States of America or to any other third country that is not subject to an adequacy decision by the European Commission, the Parties hereby agree to enter into the Standard Contractual Clauses as set forth in Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914 of 4 June 2021 on standard contractual clauses for the transfer of personal data to third countries pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council. The applicable Standard Contractual Clauses are Module 2 (Transfer Controller to Processor), and such SCCs are incorporated by reference into this DPA as if set forth herein in full. The completed Annexes to the Standard Contractual Clauses, including the description of the transfer, the technical and organizational measures, and the list of Subprocessors, are set forth in Annex A to this DPA. In the event of any conflict between the Standard Contractual Clauses and any other provision of this DPA, the Standard Contractual Clauses shall prevail to the extent of the conflict.
164: 
165: **7.3** The Processor shall cooperate with the Controller in good faith to ensure that appropriate and legally sufficient safeguards are in place for any international transfer of Personal Data carried out in connection with the Services, including any transfers that may arise from changes in applicable law, regulatory guidance, or judicial decisions affecting the validity or adequacy of existing transfer mechanisms. The Processor shall promptly inform the Controller if, in the Processor\'s reasonable opinion, any existing transfer safeguard is or may become insufficient to ensure lawful transfers under Applicable Data Protection Law.
166: 
167: **[SECTION 8 --- DATA SUBJECT RIGHTS]{.underline}**
168: 
169: **8.1** The Processor shall, taking into account the nature of the Processing, assist the Controller by appropriate technical and organizational measures, insofar as this is possible, for the fulfilment of the Controller\'s obligation to respond to requests for exercising the rights of Data Subjects under Chapter III of the GDPR (Articles 15 through 22). Such Data Subject rights include, without limitation:
170: 
171: > \(a\) The right of access (Article 15 GDPR);
172: >
173: > \(b\) The right to rectification (Article 16 GDPR);
174: >
175: > \(c\) The right to erasure (\"right to be forgotten\") (Article 17 GDPR);
176: >
177: > \(d\) The right to restriction of processing (Article 18 GDPR);
178: >
179: > \(e\) The notification obligation regarding rectification, erasure, or restriction (Article 19 GDPR);
180: >
181: > \(f\) The right to data portability (Article 20 GDPR);
182: >
183: > \(g\) The right to object (Article 21 GDPR); and
184: >
185: > \(h\) The right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling (Article 22 GDPR).
186: 
187: **8.2** The Processor shall promptly, and in any event within five (5) business days, notify the Controller if the Processor receives a request from a Data Subject directly in relation to the Controller\'s Personal Data. The Processor shall not respond to any such Data Subject request itself unless expressly authorized in writing by the Controller to do so. The Processor shall provide the Controller with a copy of the Data Subject request and any information reasonably necessary to assist the Controller in evaluating and responding to the request.
188: 
189: **8.3** The Processor shall provide substantive assistance to the Controller in responding to Data Subject requests within ten (10) business days of the Controller\'s written request for such assistance. Such assistance may include, as applicable, searching the Processor\'s systems for the relevant Personal Data, providing copies of Personal Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format, implementing restrictions on Processing, or effecting the erasure of Personal Data from the Processor\'s systems. The Controller acknowledges that the Processor\'s ability to assist may depend on the nature of the Services and the architecture of the Processor\'s systems.
190: 
191: **8.4** To the extent that the Processor incurs material costs in providing assistance under this Section 8 beyond what is reasonably anticipated in the ordinary course of the Services, the Processor may charge the Controller reasonable fees for such assistance, based on the Processor\'s then-current professional services rates, provided that the Processor has obtained the Controller\'s prior written approval for any such charges.
192: 
193: **[SECTION 9 --- PERSONAL DATA BREACH NOTIFICATION]{.underline}**
194: 
195: **9.1** The Processor shall notify the Controller of any Personal Data Breach without undue delay and in any event no later than forty-eight (48) hours after becoming aware of the Personal Data Breach. For the purposes of this Section 9, the Processor shall be deemed to have become \"aware\" of a Personal Data Breach when the Processor\'s incident response team or any member of the Processor\'s management has confirmed, following initial assessment, that a security incident constitutes a Personal Data Breach within the meaning of Article 4(12) of the GDPR. The Processor shall maintain documented procedures to ensure that potential Personal Data Breaches are identified, escalated, and assessed promptly.
196: 
197: **9.2** The notification provided under Section 9.1 shall include, to the extent such information is available at the time of notification and to the extent it can be provided without unreasonable delay:
198: 
199: > \(a\) A description of the nature of the Personal Data Breach, including, where possible, the categories and approximate number of Data Subjects concerned and the categories and approximate number of Personal Data records concerned;
200: >
201: > \(b\) The name and contact details of the Processor\'s Data Protection Officer (or, if the Data Protection Officer is unavailable, another designated contact point) where more information can be obtained regarding the Personal Data Breach;
202: >
203: > \(c\) A description of the likely consequences of the Personal Data Breach, including an assessment of the potential risks to the rights and freedoms of affected Data Subjects;
204: >
205: > \(d\) A description of the measures taken or proposed to be taken by the Processor to address the Personal Data Breach, including, where appropriate, measures to contain the breach, mitigate its possible adverse effects, and prevent recurrence.
206: 
207: **9.3** Where, and to the extent that, it is not possible to provide all of the information specified in Section 9.2 at the same time as the initial notification, the Processor shall provide such information in phases without undue further delay as additional information becomes available. The Processor shall provide supplemental notifications to the Controller as soon as reasonably practicable and in any event shall endeavor to provide complete information within seventy-two (72) hours of the initial notification.
208: 
209: **9.4** The Processor shall document all Personal Data Breaches, including the facts relating to the Personal Data Breach, its effects, and the remedial action taken, in accordance with Article 33(5) of the GDPR. Such documentation shall be maintained for a period of not less than three (3) years from the date of the Personal Data Breach and shall be made available to the Controller upon request.
210: 
211: **9.5** The Processor shall cooperate with and assist the Controller in the Controller\'s performance of its obligations under Articles 33 and 34 of the GDPR, including the Controller\'s obligation to notify the competent Supervisory Authority and, where applicable, to communicate the Personal Data Breach to affected Data Subjects. The Processor shall provide such cooperation and assistance promptly and in a manner that enables the Controller to meet the applicable notification timelines under the GDPR.
212: 
213: **9.6** In the event that the Processor fails to provide the initial notification of a Personal Data Breach within the forty-eight (48) hour timeline specified in Section 9.1, the Processor shall pay to the Controller a penalty of one thousand Euros (€1,000) per calendar day of delay commencing on the date that is forty-eight (48) hours after the Processor became aware of the Personal Data Breach and continuing until the date on which notification is actually provided to the Controller, provided that such penalty shall not exceed fifty thousand Euros (€50,000) in the aggregate per breach incident. The Parties acknowledge that such penalties represent a genuine pre-estimate of the Controller\'s loss resulting from delayed notification and are not intended as punitive damages.
214: 
215: **9.7** The obligations set forth in this Section 9 are without prejudice to any other rights, remedies, or claims the Controller may have under this DPA, the Agreement, or applicable law in connection with a Personal Data Breach.
216: 
217: **[SECTION 10 --- DATA PROTECTION IMPACT ASSESSMENTS]{.underline}**
218: 
219: **10.1** The Processor shall provide reasonable assistance to the Controller in the conduct of data protection impact assessments (\"DPIAs\") pursuant to Article 35 of the GDPR, where the Controller determines that a type of Processing is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons. The Processor shall also provide reasonable assistance to the Controller in connection with prior consultations with the competent Supervisory Authority pursuant to Article 36 of the GDPR, where the results of a DPIA indicate that the Processing would result in a high risk in the absence of measures taken by the Controller to mitigate the risk. In each case, the Processor\'s obligation to provide assistance shall take into account the nature of the Processing activities and the information available to the Processor.
220: 
221: **10.2** Such assistance shall include, without limitation, providing the Controller with information regarding the Processor\'s technical and organizational measures as described in Annex B, the Processing activities carried out on behalf of the Controller as described in Annex A, the results of any security assessments, penetration tests, or audits conducted by or on behalf of the Processor, and such other information as is reasonably necessary for the Controller to conduct a comprehensive DPIA. The Processor shall respond to the Controller\'s reasonable requests for information in connection with a DPIA within a reasonable timeframe, and in any event within twenty (20) business days of the Controller\'s request.
222: 
223: **10.3** The Processor may charge reasonable fees for assistance provided under this Section 10, based on the Processor\'s then-current professional services rates and the scope and complexity of the assistance requested. The Processor shall provide the Controller with a fee estimate prior to commencing any such assistance and shall obtain the Controller\'s written approval before incurring fees in excess of five thousand Euros (€5,000) for any single DPIA engagement.
224: 
225: **[SECTION 11 --- AUDIT RIGHTS]{.underline}**
226: 
227: **11.1** The Processor shall make available to the Controller all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with the obligations laid down in Article 28 of the GDPR and this DPA, and shall allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by the Controller or another auditor mandated by the Controller, in accordance with Article 28(3)(h) of the GDPR. The Processor shall cooperate in good faith with the Controller in connection with any such audit and shall provide the Controller\'s audit team with reasonable access to relevant documentation, systems, and personnel.
228: 
229: **11.2** The Controller may conduct an audit of the Processor\'s Processing activities no more than once per calendar year, subject to at least thirty (30) calendar days\' prior written notice to the Processor. Audits shall be conducted during the Processor\'s normal business hours (Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Central European Time, excluding German public holidays) and shall not unreasonably interfere with the Processor\'s business operations or the Processor\'s obligations to its other customers. The Controller\'s audit team shall comply with the Processor\'s reasonable security and confidentiality requirements while on the Processor\'s premises.
230: 
231: **11.3** Audits conducted under Section 11.2 shall be limited to the Processor\'s primary data processing facility located in Frankfurt, Germany. The scope of each audit shall be limited to the Processing activities performed by the Processor on behalf of the Controller and shall not extend to the confidential information of the Processor\'s other customers or to systems that do not Process the Controller\'s Personal Data.
232: 
233: **11.4** The Processor may, at its sole discretion, satisfy the Controller\'s audit requests in whole or in part by providing the Controller with one or more of the following:
234: 
235: > \(a\) A current SOC 2 Type II report prepared by Clearwater Audit Partners GmbH (or a successor firm that is a nationally or internationally recognized independent audit firm) covering the Processor\'s controls relevant to the Services provided to the Controller; and/or
236: >
237: > \(b\) A current ISO 27001 certification report or certificate issued by an accredited certification body, demonstrating the Processor\'s compliance with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 or its successor standard.
238: 
239: **11.5** For reference, the most recent SOC 2 Type II report available as of the date of this DPA was dated September 30, 2024, covering the audit period from October 1, 2023 through September 30, 2024, and was issued by Clearwater Audit Partners GmbH. The Processor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain an updated SOC 2 Type II report on an annual basis and shall make the most recent report available to the Controller within thirty (30) calendar days of the Controller\'s written request.
240: 
241: **11.6** The Controller shall bear all costs and expenses associated with any audit conducted under this Section 11, including without limitation travel, accommodation, and professional fees for the Controller\'s audit team or mandated auditors, unless the audit reveals a material breach of this DPA by the Processor, in which case the Processor shall reimburse the Controller for the reasonable and documented costs of the audit, up to a maximum of twenty-five thousand Euros (€25,000) per audit.
242: 
243: **[SECTION 12 --- DATA DELETION]{.underline}**
244: 
245: **12.1** Upon termination or expiration of the Agreement for any reason, the Processor shall, at the Controller\'s choice and subject to Section 12.2, delete all Personal Data Processed on behalf of the Controller, including all copies, backups, and archives thereof, within ninety (90) calendar days of the effective date of termination or expiration of the Agreement. Deletion shall be performed using industry-standard secure deletion methods that render the Personal Data unrecoverable, including, where applicable, cryptographic erasure, multi-pass overwriting, or physical destruction of storage media.
246: 
247: **12.2** Notwithstanding Section 12.1, the Processor may retain Personal Data to the extent and for the duration required by European Union or German federal or state law to which the Processor is subject, including without limitation any mandatory data retention obligations under German commercial law (*Handelsgesetzbuch*) or German tax law (*Abgabenordnung*). In such cases, the Processor shall promptly inform the Controller of the applicable legal requirement and the categories of Personal Data to be retained, and shall limit its Processing of the retained Personal Data strictly to the purposes required by such law. The Processor shall ensure that retained Personal Data is subject to the confidentiality and security obligations set forth in this DPA for the duration of its retention.
248: 
249: **12.3** Upon request by the Controller following the completion of deletion under Section 12.1, the Processor shall provide written confirmation of the deletion of the Controller\'s Personal Data, signed by an authorized officer of the Processor. Such confirmation shall specify the date of deletion, the categories of data deleted, and the deletion methods used. The Processor shall provide such confirmation within thirty (30) calendar days of the Controller\'s request.
250: 
251: **12.4** The Controller acknowledges that deletion of Personal Data from the Processor\'s backup systems may require additional time beyond the ninety (90) calendar day period specified in Section 12.1 due to the Processor\'s automated backup rotation cycles. In such cases, the Processor shall ensure that all Personal Data is deleted from backup systems within one hundred eighty (180) calendar days of the effective date of termination or expiration, and shall isolate and restrict access to such backup copies pending their deletion.
252: 
253: **[SECTION 13 --- LIABILITY]{.underline}**
254: 
255: **13.1** The Processor\'s aggregate liability for all claims of any kind arising under or in connection with this DPA, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or otherwise, shall not exceed five hundred thousand Euros (€500,000). This limitation applies to the aggregate of all claims arising under or in connection with this DPA, regardless of the number of events, incidents, or claims giving rise to such liability.
256: 
257: **13.2** In no event shall the Processor be liable for any indirect, incidental, consequential, special, punitive, or exemplary damages arising out of or related to this DPA, including but not limited to loss of revenue, loss of profits, loss of business or anticipated savings, loss of goodwill, loss of data or corruption of data, or cost of procurement of substitute services, regardless of the theory of liability and even if the Processor has been advised of the possibility of such damages or should have foreseen the possibility thereof. This exclusion of consequential damages shall apply to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law.
258: 
259: **13.3** The limitations and exclusions set forth in this Section 13 shall apply to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law and shall survive the termination or expiration of this DPA. The Parties acknowledge that the limitations and exclusions set forth in this Section 13 reflect a fair and reasonable allocation of risk between the Parties, taking into account the nature of the Services, the fees payable under the Agreement, and the respective responsibilities of the Parties under this DPA and applicable law.
260: 
261: **13.4** Nothing in this Section 13 shall limit the Processor\'s liability for damages caused by a failure to comply with its obligations under the GDPR specifically directed to processors, or for damages caused to Data Subjects arising from the Processor\'s non-compliance with its obligations under Article 82 of the GDPR. Article 82 of the GDPR provides that any processor involved in processing shall be liable for damage caused by processing only where it has not complied with obligations of the GDPR specifically directed to processors, or where it has acted outside of or contrary to lawful instructions of the controller.
262: 
263: **13.5** For the avoidance of doubt, each Party shall be liable for the entirety of the damage suffered by a Data Subject in accordance with Article 82(4) of the GDPR, subject to any right of recourse between the Parties as provided in Article 82(5) of the GDPR. Where a Party has paid full compensation for the damage suffered, that Party shall be entitled to claim back from the other Party that part of the compensation corresponding to the other Party\'s share of responsibility for the damage.
264: 
265: **[SECTION 14 --- GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION]{.underline}**
266: 
267: **14.1** This DPA and any disputes arising out of or in connection with this DPA, including disputes regarding the existence, validity, interpretation, performance, breach, or termination of this DPA, and including any non-contractual claims arising out of or in connection with this DPA, shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, without regard to its conflict of laws principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction. To the extent that the GDPR or other mandatory provisions of European Union law apply to any matter arising under this DPA, such provisions shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions of German national law.
268: 
269: **14.2** Any dispute arising out of or in connection with this DPA that the Parties are unable to resolve through good-faith negotiations within thirty (30) calendar days of one Party\'s written notice to the other Party describing the nature of the dispute and the relief sought, shall be finally settled by arbitration administered by the Deutsche Institution für Schiedsgerichtsbarkeit e.V. (\"DIS\") in accordance with the DIS Arbitration Rules (DIS-Schiedsgerichtsordnung) in effect at the time of the commencement of the arbitration proceedings. The seat of arbitration shall be Munich, Germany. The language of the arbitration proceedings shall be English. The arbitral tribunal shall consist of three (3) arbitrators, with each Party nominating one arbitrator and the two Party-nominated arbitrators selecting the presiding arbitrator. If the two Party-nominated arbitrators fail to agree on the selection of the presiding arbitrator within thirty (30) calendar days of the appointment of the second Party-nominated arbitrator, the presiding arbitrator shall be appointed by the DIS Appointing Authority in accordance with the DIS Arbitration Rules.
270: 
271: **14.3** The arbitral tribunal shall have the authority to award any remedy or relief that a court of competent jurisdiction could grant, including but not limited to monetary damages, declaratory relief, and specific performance, provided that the arbitral tribunal shall not have the authority to award punitive or exemplary damages except to the extent that such damages are recoverable under Article 82 of the GDPR or other mandatory provisions of applicable law.
272: 
273: **14.4** Nothing in this Section 14 shall prevent either Party from seeking interim, provisional, or injunctive relief from any court of competent jurisdiction, including courts in Germany or any other jurisdiction, where such relief is necessary to prevent irreparable harm or to preserve the status quo pending the resolution of a dispute through arbitration. Any application for interim or injunctive relief shall not be deemed a waiver of the right to arbitrate.
274: 
275: **14.5** All arbitration proceedings and any arbitral award shall be kept strictly confidential by the Parties and the arbitrators, except to the extent that disclosure is required by applicable law, by a Supervisory Authority, or in connection with the enforcement of an arbitral award.
276: 
277: **[SECTION 15 --- DATA PROTECTION OFFICER]{.underline}**
278: 
279: **15.1** The Processor has appointed a Data Protection Officer in accordance with Articles 37 through 39 of the GDPR. As of the date of this DPA, the Processor\'s designated Data Protection Officer is:
280: 
281: > **Dr. Annika Vogt** Data Protection Officer Stratosphere Cloud Services GmbH Hohenzollernstraße 88 80796 Munich, Germany
282: >
283: > Email: dpo@stratospherecloud.example.com
284: >
285: > Telephone: +49 89 2155 4450
286: 
287: **15.2** The Controller may direct data protection inquiries, requests, or complaints related to the Processing of Personal Data under this DPA to the Processor\'s Data Protection Officer at the contact details set forth above. The Processor shall ensure that the Data Protection Officer is available to respond to the Controller\'s inquiries within a reasonable timeframe and, in any event, within ten (10) business days of receipt of a written inquiry.
288: 
289: **15.3** The Processor shall promptly notify the Controller in writing of any change in the identity or contact details of its Data Protection Officer, and in any event within fifteen (15) calendar days of such change.
290: 
291: **[SECTION 16 --- TERM AND SURVIVAL]{.underline}**
292: 
293: **16.1** This DPA shall become effective on the date of its execution by both Parties (the \"Effective Date\") and shall remain in full force and effect for the duration of the Agreement, including any renewals, extensions, or amendments thereof, for so long as the Processor Processes Personal Data on behalf of the Controller.
294: 
295: **16.2** This DPA shall automatically terminate upon the termination or expiration of the Agreement, subject to the survival provisions set forth in Section 16.3 below and the Processor\'s obligations under Section 12 (Data Deletion).
296: 
297: **16.3** Notwithstanding the termination or expiration of this DPA, the following provisions shall survive and remain in full force and effect for a period of two (2) years following the effective date of termination or expiration:
298: 
299: > \(a\) Section 9 (Personal Data Breach Notification), to the extent the Processor discovers a Personal Data Breach relating to the Controller\'s Personal Data during the survival period;
300: >
301: > \(b\) Section 11 (Audit Rights), to the extent necessary for the Controller to verify the Processor\'s compliance with its post-termination obligations, including its obligations under Section 12;
302: >
303: > \(c\) Section 12 (Data Deletion), including the Processor\'s obligation to delete Personal Data and to provide written confirmation of such deletion;
304: >
305: > \(d\) Section 13 (Liability), with respect to any claims arising under or in connection with this DPA, whether such claims accrue before, on, or after the date of termination or expiration.
306: 
307: **16.4** The survival period specified in Section 16.3 shall commence on the effective date of termination or expiration of this DPA. Upon the expiration of the survival period, the surviving provisions shall cease to have effect, except to the extent that applicable law requires continued compliance with any obligation set forth therein.
308: 
309: **16.5** The provisions of Section 4 (Confidentiality) shall survive the termination or expiration of this DPA indefinitely in accordance with Section 4.3.
310: 
311: **[SECTION 17 --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**
312: 
313: **17.1 Entire Agreement.** This DPA, together with its Annexes and the Agreement, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, understandings, negotiations, and discussions, whether oral or written, between the Parties relating to the Processing of Personal Data in connection with the Services.
314: 
315: **17.2 Amendments.** No amendment, modification, or supplement to this DPA shall be effective unless it is in writing and signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Processor may update Annex B (Technical and Organizational Measures) from time to time in accordance with Section 5.5 of this DPA.

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, the Controller and the Processor have entered into a Master Services Agreement dated \\*\\*\\*\\*\\*\\*\\*\\*\\*\\*\\*\\*\\*\\*\\*\\* (the \"Agreement\") pursuant to which the Processor provides cloud hosting, managed database services, and analytics support to the Controller in connection with the Controller\'s business operations;

**WHEREAS**, in the course of providing the Services under the Agreement, the Processor will Process Personal Data on behalf of the Controller, and such Processing may involve the collection, storage, retrieval, use, disclosure by transmission, combination, restriction, erasure, and destruction of Personal Data as further described in Annex A to this DPA;

**WHEREAS**, the Parties wish to ensure that such Processing of Personal Data complies with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data, and repealing Directive 95/46/EC (the \"General Data Protection Regulation\" or \"GDPR\"), as well as applicable data protection laws of the European Union and its Member States;

**WHEREAS**, the Parties intend for this DPA to set forth their respective obligations with respect to the Processing of Personal Data in connection with the Agreement, including without limitation the Processor\'s obligations as a data processor within the meaning of Article 4(8) and Article 28 of the GDPR; and

**WHEREAS**, the Parties agree that this DPA, together with the Annexes attached hereto, constitutes the binding agreement between them with respect to the Processing of Personal Data under the Agreement and shall supplement and form an integral part of the Agreement;

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual obligations set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
**[SECTION 1 --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

**1.1** \"**Applicable Data Protection Law**\" means Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (the GDPR) and any applicable legislation of the European Union or its Member States implementing, supplementing, or replacing the GDPR, including without limitation the German Federal Data Protection Act (*Bundesdatenschutzgesetz*, \"BDSG\") as amended from time to time, and any other data protection legislation directly applicable within the European Economic Area.

**1.2** \"**Controller**\" means the natural or legal person, public authority, agency, or other body which, alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of the Processing of Personal Data, as defined in Article 4(7) of the GDPR, and as identified in the signature block of this DPA.

**1.3** \"**Data Subject**\" means an identified or identifiable natural person to whom Personal Data relates, as defined in Article 4(1) of the GDPR. An identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data, an online identifier, or to one or more factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural, or social identity of that natural person.
**1.4** \"**EEA**\" means the European Economic Area, comprising the Member States of the European Union together with Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway.

**1.5** \"**Personal Data**\" means any information relating to a Data Subject, as defined in Article 4(1) of the GDPR. For the purposes of this DPA, Personal Data includes all categories of data described in Annex A to this DPA that are Processed by the Processor on behalf of the Controller in connection with the Services.

**1.6** \"**Personal Data Breach**\" means a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorized disclosure of, or access to, Personal Data transmitted, stored, or otherwise Processed, as defined in Article 4(12) of the GDPR.

**1.7** \"**Processing**\" (and its cognates \"**Process**,\" \"**Processed**,\" and \"**Processes**\") means any operation or set of operations which is performed on Personal Data or on sets of Personal Data, whether or not by automated means, such as collection, recording, organization, structuring, storage, adaptation or alteration, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure by transmission, dissemination or otherwise making available, alignment or combination, restriction, erasure, or destruction, as defined in Article 4(2) of the GDPR.

**1.8** \"**Processor**\" means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency, or other body which Processes Personal Data on behalf of the Controller, as defined in Article 4(8) of the GDPR. For the purposes of this DPA, the Processor is Stratosphere Cloud Services GmbH.

**1.9** \"**Standard Contractual Clauses**\" or \"**SCCs**\" means the standard contractual clauses for the transfer of personal data to third countries pursuant to Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914 of 4 June 2021 on standard contractual clauses for the transfer of personal data to third countries pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council, as may be amended, supplemented, or replaced from time to time by the European Commission.

**1.10** \"**Subprocessor**\" means any third party engaged by the Processor (or by any subsequent Subprocessor of the Processor) to Process Personal Data on behalf of the Controller in connection with the Services provided under the Agreement.

**1.11** \"**Supervisory Authority**\" means an independent public authority which is established by a Member State of the European Union pursuant to Article 51 of the GDPR and which is responsible for monitoring the application of the GDPR in order to protect the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons in relation to Processing.

**1.12** \"**Technical and Organizational Measures**\" or \"**TOMs**\" means the technical and organizational security measures implemented by the Processor to protect Personal Data against accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorized disclosure, or access, as more particularly described in Annex B to this DPA.

**1.13** Unless otherwise defined herein, capitalized terms used in this DPA shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Agreement or in the GDPR, as applicable. In the event of a conflict between the definitions in this DPA and the definitions in the Agreement, the definitions in this DPA shall prevail to the extent they relate to data protection matters.
**[SECTION 2 --- SCOPE OF PROCESSING]{.underline}**

**2.1** This DPA applies to all Processing of Personal Data by the Processor on behalf of the Controller pursuant to the Agreement. The scope of this DPA encompasses all Services provided under the Agreement to the extent that such Services involve the Processing of Personal Data, regardless of the geographic location of the data processing infrastructure used by the Processor or its Subprocessors in connection with the delivery of such Services.

**2.2** The details of the Processing, including the subject matter and duration of the Processing, the nature and purpose of the Processing, the types of Personal Data Processed, and the categories of Data Subjects whose Personal Data is Processed, are set forth in Annex A (Description of Processing) to this DPA. Annex A forms an integral part of this DPA and is incorporated herein by reference. The Controller and the Processor may amend Annex A from time to time by mutual written agreement to reflect changes in the Processing activities under the Agreement.

**2.3** This DPA shall take precedence over any conflicting or inconsistent terms in the Agreement with respect to the Processing of Personal Data. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the terms of this DPA and the terms of the Agreement as they relate to the protection, security, or Processing of Personal Data, the terms of this DPA shall control.

**2.4** For the avoidance of doubt, this DPA does not relieve the Controller of its obligations under Applicable Data Protection Law, including its obligations as a data controller under the GDPR. The Controller remains responsible for determining the lawfulness of the Processing instructions it provides to the Processor and for ensuring that a valid legal basis exists for each Processing activity described in Annex A.
**[SECTION 3 --- CONTROLLER INSTRUCTIONS]{.underline}**

**3.1** The Processor shall Process Personal Data only on documented instructions from the Controller, including with regard to transfers of Personal Data to a third country or an international organization, unless required to do so by European Union or Member State law to which the Processor is subject. In such a case, the Processor shall inform the Controller of that legal requirement before carrying out the Processing, unless that law prohibits such information on important grounds of public interest, in accordance with Article 28(3)(a) of the GDPR. The Processor acknowledges that the requirement to Process on documented instructions is a fundamental obligation under this DPA and the GDPR.

**3.2** The Processor shall immediately inform the Controller if, in the Processor\'s opinion, an instruction provided by the Controller infringes the GDPR or other European Union or Member State data protection provisions. The Processor shall have no obligation to independently assess whether the Controller\'s instructions comply with Applicable Data Protection Law, but shall not knowingly carry out an instruction that it believes to be in clear violation of the GDPR. Upon informing the Controller of a potential infringement, the Processor shall be entitled to suspend the performance of the relevant instruction until the Controller confirms or modifies the instruction in writing.

**3.3** The Agreement, this DPA (including all Annexes hereto), and any additional written instructions provided by the Controller from time to time in accordance with the Agreement, together constitute the Controller\'s complete and documented instructions to the Processor with respect to the Processing of Personal Data as of the date of execution of this DPA. Any additional or modified instructions shall be documented in writing and agreed upon by the Parties. The Processor shall not be required to comply with any instruction that is inconsistent with the terms of the Agreement or this DPA unless such instruction is formalized through an amendment executed by both Parties.

**3.4** The Controller warrants that its instructions to the Processor, including the Processing activities described in Annex A, have a lawful basis under Applicable Data Protection Law, including where applicable a valid legal basis under Article 6 of the GDPR and, with respect to special categories of data, a valid condition under Article 9 of the GDPR.
**[SECTION 4 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

**4.1** The Processor shall ensure that all persons authorized to Process Personal Data on behalf of the Controller, including the Processor\'s employees, contractors, temporary workers, and agents, have committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality, in accordance with Article 28(3)(b) of the GDPR. The Processor shall maintain written records of such confidentiality commitments and shall make them available to the Controller upon request.

**4.2** The Processor shall ensure that access to Personal Data Processed on behalf of the Controller is strictly limited to those members of the Processor\'s personnel who require such access for the performance of the Services under the Agreement. The Processor shall implement appropriate access management procedures, including role-based access controls and least-privilege principles, to enforce this limitation. The Processor shall promptly revoke access for any personnel member whose role no longer requires access to the Controller\'s Personal Data.

**4.3** The obligations set forth in this Section 4 shall survive the termination or expiration of this DPA and shall continue in full force and effect for so long as the Processor or any of its personnel retains any Personal Data Processed on behalf of the Controller.

**4.4** The Processor shall not disclose Personal Data to any third party, including any governmental authority or body, except as expressly authorized by the Controller in writing, as required by applicable European Union or Member State law, or as otherwise permitted under this DPA (including disclosure to authorized Subprocessors in accordance with Section 6).
**[SECTION 5 --- SECURITY OF PROCESSING]{.underline}**

**5.1** The Processor shall implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk presented by the Processing, in accordance with Article 32 of the GDPR. In determining the appropriate level of security, the Processor shall take into account the state of the art, the costs of implementation, and the nature, scope, context, and purposes of Processing, as well as the risk of varying likelihood and severity for the rights and freedoms of the natural persons whose Personal Data is Processed. The Processor acknowledges that the Personal Data Processed under this DPA includes special categories of data (health data) and shall ensure that the security measures reflect the heightened sensitivity of such data.

**5.2** The technical and organizational measures implemented by the Processor are described in detail in Annex B (Technical and Organizational Measures) to this DPA, which forms an integral part of this DPA and is incorporated herein by reference. Without limiting the generality of Section 5.1, such measures include, as of the date of this DPA:
> \(a\) Encryption of Personal Data at rest using the Advanced Encryption Standard with 256-bit keys (AES-256) across all data storage systems and media utilized in the delivery of the Services;

> \(b\) Encryption of Personal Data in transit using Transport Layer Security version 1.3 (TLS 1.3) for all data transmissions between the Controller\'s systems and the Processor\'s infrastructure, as well as between the Processor\'s data centers and between the Processor and its Subprocessors;

> \(c\) Logical access controls, including role-based access control (RBAC) with least-privilege principles, multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all administrative and privileged access, and segregation of duties for critical Processing activities;

> \(d\) Annual penetration testing conducted by an independent third-party information security firm, with findings reported to the Processor\'s Chief Information Security Officer and remediation tracked to completion;
> \(e\) Intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDS/IPS) deployed across all network segments and monitored on a continuous 24/7 basis by the Processor\'s security operations center;

> \(f\) Regular vulnerability scanning conducted on a monthly basis, with critical and high-severity vulnerabilities remediated within timeframes established by the Processor\'s vulnerability management policy, and a formalized patch management program.

**5.3** The Processor shall regularly test, assess, and evaluate the effectiveness of its technical and organizational measures for ensuring the security of Processing, in accordance with Article 32(1)(d) of the GDPR. Such testing and evaluation shall be conducted at least annually and shall include, at a minimum, the penetration testing and vulnerability scanning described in Section 5.2(d) and (f) above.

**5.4** The Processor holds ISO 27001:2022 certification, Certificate Number ISO-27001-SC-2024-0891, issued by TÜV Rheinland AG on June 15, 2024, valid through June 14, 2027. The Processor shall maintain ISO 27001 certification (or an equivalent internationally recognized information security management system certification) throughout the term of this DPA. The Processor shall promptly notify the Controller if its ISO 27001 certification is suspended, withdrawn, or not renewed, and shall provide the Controller with a remediation plan within thirty (30) calendar days of any such event.

**5.5** The Processor shall not materially diminish the overall level of security provided by its technical and organizational measures during the term of this DPA. The Processor may update or modify its technical and organizational measures from time to time, provided that any such update or modification does not result in a material reduction in the level of security afforded to the Controller\'s Personal Data. The Processor shall update Annex B to reflect any material changes to its technical and organizational measures and shall provide the updated Annex B to the Controller within thirty (30) calendar days of such changes.

**[SECTION 7 --- INTERNATIONAL DATA TRANSFERS]{.underline}**

**7.1** The Processor shall not transfer Personal Data to any country or territory outside the European Economic Area (\"EEA\") or to any international organization, and shall not permit any Subprocessor to make any such transfer, unless one of the following conditions is satisfied:

> \(a\) The European Commission has issued an adequacy decision for the recipient country, territory, or international organization, or a specified sector within such country, pursuant to Article 45 of the GDPR, and such adequacy decision remains in force and has not been invalidated by the Court of Justice of the European Union or otherwise;

> \(b\) Appropriate safeguards have been provided in accordance with Article 46 of the GDPR, including but not limited to the execution of Standard Contractual Clauses approved by the European Commission, the adoption of binding corporate rules approved by a competent Supervisory Authority, or the use of an approved certification mechanism together with binding and enforceable commitments of the data importer; or

> \(c\) A derogation for specific situations under Article 49 of the GDPR applies, provided that such derogation is interpreted restrictively in accordance with the guidance of the European Data Protection Board.

**7.2** To the extent that the Processing involves transfers of Personal Data from the EEA to the United States of America or to any other third country that is not subject to an adequacy decision by the European Commission, the Parties hereby agree to enter into the Standard Contractual Clauses as set forth in Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914 of 4 June 2021 on standard contractual clauses for the transfer of personal data to third countries pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council. The applicable Standard Contractual Clauses are Module 2 (Transfer Controller to Processor), and such SCCs are incorporated by reference into this DPA as if set forth herein in full. The completed Annexes to the Standard Contractual Clauses, including the description of the transfer, the technical and organizational measures, and the list of Subprocessors, are set forth in Annex A to this DPA. In the event of any conflict between the Standard Contractual Clauses and any other provision of this DPA, the Standard Contractual Clauses shall prevail to the extent of the conflict.

**7.3** The Processor shall cooperate with the Controller in good faith to ensure that appropriate and legally sufficient safeguards are in place for any international transfer of Personal Data carried out in connection with the Services, including any transfers that may arise from changes in applicable law, regulatory guidance, or judicial decisions affecting the validity or adequacy of existing transfer mechanisms. The Processor shall promptly inform the Controller if, in the Processor\'s reasonable opinion, any existing transfer safeguard is or may become insufficient to ensure lawful transfers under Applicable Data Protection Law.
**[SECTION 8 --- DATA SUBJECT RIGHTS]{.underline}**

**8.1** The Processor shall, taking into account the nature of the Processing, assist the Controller by appropriate technical and organizational measures, insofar as this is possible, for the fulfilment of the Controller\'s obligation to respond to requests for exercising the rights of Data Subjects under Chapter III of the GDPR (Articles 15 through 22). Such Data Subject rights include, without limitation:
> \(a\) The right of access (Article 15 GDPR);
> \(b\) The right to rectification (Article 16 GDPR);
> \(c\) The right to erasure (\"right to be forgotten\") (Article 17 GDPR);
> \(d\) The right to restriction of processing (Article 18 GDPR);
> \(e\) The notification obligation regarding rectification, erasure, or restriction (Article 19 GDPR);
> \(f\) The right to data portability (Article 20 GDPR);
> \(g\) The right to object (Article 21 GDPR); and
> \(h\) The right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling (Article 22 GDPR).

**8.2** The Processor shall promptly, and in any event within five (5) business days, notify the Controller if the Processor receives a request from a Data Subject directly in relation to the Controller\'s Personal Data. The Processor shall not respond to any such Data Subject request itself unless expressly authorized in writing by the Controller to do so. The Processor shall provide the Controller with a copy of the Data Subject request and any information reasonably necessary to assist the Controller in evaluating and responding to the request.

**8.3** The Processor shall provide substantive assistance to the Controller in responding to Data Subject requests within ten (10) business days of the Controller\'s written request for such assistance. Such assistance may include, as applicable, searching the Processor\'s systems for the relevant Personal Data, providing copies of Personal Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format, implementing restrictions on Processing, or effecting the erasure of Personal Data from the Processor\'s systems. The Controller acknowledges that the Processor\'s ability to assist may depend on the nature of the Services and the architecture of the Processor\'s systems.

**8.4** To the extent that the Processor incurs material costs in providing assistance under this Section 8 beyond what is reasonably anticipated in the ordinary course of the Services, the Processor may charge the Controller reasonable fees for such assistance, based on the Processor\'s then-current professional services rates, provided that the Processor has obtained the Controller\'s prior written approval for any such charges.
**[SECTION 9 --- PERSONAL DATA BREACH NOTIFICATION]{.underline}**

**9.1** The Processor shall notify the Controller of any Personal Data Breach without undue delay and in any event no later than forty-eight (48) hours after becoming aware of the Personal Data Breach. For the purposes of this Section 9, the Processor shall be deemed to have become \"aware\" of a Personal Data Breach when the Processor\'s incident response team or any member of the Processor\'s management has confirmed, following initial assessment, that a security incident constitutes a Personal Data Breach within the meaning of Article 4(12) of the GDPR. The Processor shall maintain documented procedures to ensure that potential Personal Data Breaches are identified, escalated, and assessed promptly.

**9.2** The notification provided under Section 9.1 shall include, to the extent such information is available at the time of notification and to the extent it can be provided without unreasonable delay:

> \(a\) A description of the nature of the Personal Data Breach, including, where possible, the categories and approximate number of Data Subjects concerned and the categories and approximate number of Personal Data records concerned;

> \(b\) The name and contact details of the Processor\'s Data Protection Officer (or, if the Data Protection Officer is unavailable, another designated contact point) where more information can be obtained regarding the Personal Data Breach;
> \(c\) A description of the likely consequences of the Personal Data Breach, including an assessment of the potential risks to the rights and freedoms of affected Data Subjects;

> \(d\) A description of the measures taken or proposed to be taken by the Processor to address the Personal Data Breach, including, where appropriate, measures to contain the breach, mitigate its possible adverse effects, and prevent recurrence.

**9.3** Where, and to the extent that, it is not possible to provide all of the information specified in Section 9.2 at the same time as the initial notification, the Processor shall provide such information in phases without undue further delay as additional information becomes available. The Processor shall provide supplemental notifications to the Controller as soon as reasonably practicable and in any event shall endeavor to provide complete information within seventy-two (72) hours of the initial notification.

**9.4** The Processor shall document all Personal Data Breaches, including the facts relating to the Personal Data Breach, its effects, and the remedial action taken, in accordance with Article 33(5) of the GDPR. Such documentation shall be maintained for a period of not less than three (3) years from the date of the Personal Data Breach and shall be made available to the Controller upon request.

**9.5** The Processor shall cooperate with and assist the Controller in the Controller\'s performance of its obligations under Articles 33 and 34 of the GDPR, including the Controller\'s obligation to notify the competent Supervisory Authority and, where applicable, to communicate the Personal Data Breach to affected Data Subjects. The Processor shall provide such cooperation and assistance promptly and in a manner that enables the Controller to meet the applicable notification timelines under the GDPR.

**9.6** In the event that the Processor fails to provide the initial notification of a Personal Data Breach within the forty-eight (48) hour timeline specified in Section 9.1, the Processor shall pay to the Controller a penalty of one thousand Euros (€1,000) per calendar day of delay commencing on the date that is forty-eight (48) hours after the Processor became aware of the Personal Data Breach and continuing until the date on which notification is actually provided to the Controller, provided that such penalty shall not exceed fifty thousand Euros (€50,000) in the aggregate per breach incident. The Parties acknowledge that such penalties represent a genuine pre-estimate of the Controller\'s loss resulting from delayed notification and are not intended as punitive damages.

**9.7** The obligations set forth in this Section 9 are without prejudice to any other rights, remedies, or claims the Controller may have under this DPA, the Agreement, or applicable law in connection with a Personal Data Breach.
**[SECTION 10 --- DATA PROTECTION IMPACT ASSESSMENTS]{.underline}**

**10.1** The Processor shall provide reasonable assistance to the Controller in the conduct of data protection impact assessments (\"DPIAs\") pursuant to Article 35 of the GDPR, where the Controller determines that a type of Processing is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons. The Processor shall also provide reasonable assistance to the Controller in connection with prior consultations with the competent Supervisory Authority pursuant to Article 36 of the GDPR, where the results of a DPIA indicate that the Processing would result in a high risk in the absence of measures taken by the Controller to mitigate the risk. In each case, the Processor\'s obligation to provide assistance shall take into account the nature of the Processing activities and the information available to the Processor.

**10.2** Such assistance shall include, without limitation, providing the Controller with information regarding the Processor\'s technical and organizational measures as described in Annex B, the Processing activities carried out on behalf of the Controller as described in Annex A, the results of any security assessments, penetration tests, or audits conducted by or on behalf of the Processor, and such other information as is reasonably necessary for the Controller to conduct a comprehensive DPIA. The Processor shall respond to the Controller\'s reasonable requests for information in connection with a DPIA within a reasonable timeframe, and in any event within twenty (20) business days of the Controller\'s request.

**10.3** The Processor may charge reasonable fees for assistance provided under this Section 10, based on the Processor\'s then-current professional services rates and the scope and complexity of the assistance requested. The Processor shall provide the Controller with a fee estimate prior to commencing any such assistance and shall obtain the Controller\'s written approval before incurring fees in excess of five thousand Euros (€5,000) for any single DPIA engagement.
**[SECTION 11 --- AUDIT RIGHTS]{.underline}**

**11.1** The Processor shall make available to the Controller all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with the obligations laid down in Article 28 of the GDPR and this DPA, and shall allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by the Controller or another auditor mandated by the Controller, in accordance with Article 28(3)(h) of the GDPR. The Processor shall cooperate in good faith with the Controller in connection with any such audit and shall provide the Controller\'s audit team with reasonable access to relevant documentation, systems, and personnel.

**11.2** The Controller may conduct an audit of the Processor\'s Processing activities no more than once per calendar year, subject to at least thirty (30) calendar days\' prior written notice to the Processor. Audits shall be conducted during the Processor\'s normal business hours (Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Central European Time, excluding German public holidays) and shall not unreasonably interfere with the Processor\'s business operations or the Processor\'s obligations to its other customers. The Controller\'s audit team shall comply with the Processor\'s reasonable security and confidentiality requirements while on the Processor\'s premises.

**11.3** Audits conducted under Section 11.2 shall be limited to the Processor\'s primary data processing facility located in Frankfurt, Germany. The scope of each audit shall be limited to the Processing activities performed by the Processor on behalf of the Controller and shall not extend to the confidential information of the Processor\'s other customers or to systems that do not Process the Controller\'s Personal Data.
**11.4** The Processor may, at its sole discretion, satisfy the Controller\'s audit requests in whole or in part by providing the Controller with one or more of the following:

> \(a\) A current SOC 2 Type II report prepared by Clearwater Audit Partners GmbH (or a successor firm that is a nationally or internationally recognized independent audit firm) covering the Processor\'s controls relevant to the Services provided to the Controller; and/or

> \(b\) A current ISO 27001 certification report or certificate issued by an accredited certification body, demonstrating the Processor\'s compliance with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 or its successor standard.

**11.5** For reference, the most recent SOC 2 Type II report available as of the date of this DPA was dated September 30, 2024, covering the audit period from October 1, 2023 through September 30, 2024, and was issued by Clearwater Audit Partners GmbH. The Processor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain an updated SOC 2 Type II report on an annual basis and shall make the most recent report available to the Controller within thirty (30) calendar days of the Controller\'s written request.

**11.6** The Controller shall bear all costs and expenses associated with any audit conducted under this Section 11, including without limitation travel, accommodation, and professional fees for the Controller\'s audit team or mandated auditors, unless the audit reveals a material breach of this DPA by the Processor, in which case the Processor shall reimburse the Controller for the reasonable and documented costs of the audit, up to a maximum of twenty-five thousand Euros (€25,000) per audit.
**[SECTION 12 --- DATA DELETION]{.underline}**

**12.1** Upon termination or expiration of the Agreement for any reason, the Processor shall, at the Controller\'s choice and subject to Section 12.2, delete all Personal Data Processed on behalf of the Controller, including all copies, backups, and archives thereof, within ninety (90) calendar days of the effective date of termination or expiration of the Agreement. Deletion shall be performed using industry-standard secure deletion methods that render the Personal Data unrecoverable, including, where applicable, cryptographic erasure, multi-pass overwriting, or physical destruction of storage media.

**12.2** Notwithstanding Section 12.1, the Processor may retain Personal Data to the extent and for the duration required by European Union or German federal or state law to which the Processor is subject, including without limitation any mandatory data retention obligations under German commercial law (*Handelsgesetzbuch*) or German tax law (*Abgabenordnung*). In such cases, the Processor shall promptly inform the Controller of the applicable legal requirement and the categories of Personal Data to be retained, and shall limit its Processing of the retained Personal Data strictly to the purposes required by such law. The Processor shall ensure that retained Personal Data is subject to the confidentiality and security obligations set forth in this DPA for the duration of its retention.

**12.3** Upon request by the Controller following the completion of deletion under Section 12.1, the Processor shall provide written confirmation of the deletion of the Controller\'s Personal Data, signed by an authorized officer of the Processor. Such confirmation shall specify the date of deletion, the categories of data deleted, and the deletion methods used. The Processor shall provide such confirmation within thirty (30) calendar days of the Controller\'s request.

**12.4** The Controller acknowledges that deletion of Personal Data from the Processor\'s backup systems may require additional time beyond the ninety (90) calendar day period specified in Section 12.1 due to the Processor\'s automated backup rotation cycles. In such cases, the Processor shall ensure that all Personal Data is deleted from backup systems within one hundred eighty (180) calendar days of the effective date of termination or expiration, and shall isolate and restrict access to such backup copies pending their deletion.
**[SECTION 13 --- LIABILITY]{.underline}**

This exclusion of consequential damages shall apply to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law.

**13.3** The limitations and exclusions set forth in this Section 13 shall apply to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law and shall survive the termination or expiration of this DPA. **13.4** Nothing in this Section 13 shall limit the Processor\'s liability for damages caused by a failure to comply with its obligations under the GDPR specifically directed to processors, or for damages caused to Data Subjects arising from the Processor\'s non-compliance with its obligations under Article 82 of the GDPR. (\"DIS\") in accordance with the DIS Arbitration Rules (DIS-Schiedsgerichtsordnung) in effect at the time of the commencement of the arbitration proceedings. **14.3** The arbitral tribunal shall have the authority to award any remedy or relief that a court of competent jurisdiction could grant, including but not limited to monetary damages, declaratory relief, and specific performance, provided that the arbitral tribunal shall not have the authority to award punitive or exemplary damages except to the extent that such damages are recoverable under Article 82 of the GDPR or other mandatory provisions of applicable law.

**14.5** All arbitration proceedings and any arbitral award shall be kept strictly confidential by the Parties and the arbitrators, except to the extent that disclosure is required by applicable law, by a Supervisory Authority, or in connection with the enforcement of an arbitral award.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Processor may update Annex B (Technical and Organizational Measures) from time to time in accordance with Section 5.5 of this DPA.
